Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State of U.P. and perused the record.

2. This Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application under section 438 Cr.P.C. has been moved by the applicant before this Court seeking Anticipatory Bail in Case Crime No. 07 of 2005, under Sections 409, 420, 467, 468, 471, 109, 120-B I.P.C. and Section 13(1)d of Prevention of Corruption Act, Police Station Tarabganj, District Gonda.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
3. As per prosecution case in brief, F.I.R. of this case was lodged on 05.02.2005 against four accused persons, namely, Vimla Devi, Babulal Ram, Devraj Singh and Devi Shaym Shukla for the alleged offence under Sections 409, 420, 467, 468, 471, 109 I.P.C. and Section 13(1)d Prevention of Shankarnath Pandey vs State Of U.P. on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187303330/
1 Corruption Act.

entities.text: Section 13(1)d Prevention of Shankarnath Pandey vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: Complicity of the applicant came into light during investigation and his statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. was also recorded.
During investigation, the applicant had preferred Writ Petition No. 1302 of (MB) 2006, in which interim protection of stay of arrest was granted to the applicant vide order dated 27.02.2006.
After culmination of investigation three Police Reports under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C. (charge-sheets) were submitted in this case.

The charge-sheet No. 29 of 2006 dated 29.09.2006 was submitted against Vimla Devi and Babulal Ram, charge-sheet No. 29A of 2006 dated 08.1.2006 was submitted against Devi Shyma Shukla and charge-sheet No. 29B of 2006 dated 17.07.2007 was submitted against the present applicant Shankarnath Pandey, on which the concerned court below took cognizance on 06.06.2014 and summoned the accused persons.

thereafter, first time on 25.01.2016, non-bailable warrant had been issued against the accused, but on account of non-appearance of the accused persons, non-bailable warrants are repeatedly being issued against them.
4. Main substratum of argument of learned counsel for the applicant is that the applicant was falsely implicated in this case.
Charge-sheet dated 17.07.2007 has been submitted against him whithout any clinching or credible evidence against him.

No cognizance was taken on the charge-sheet of the applicant and first time on 04.02.2019, non-bailable warrant has been issued against the applicant,
but applicant was not aware about the same.
As soon as applicant came to know about the criminal proceeding and non-bailable warrant against him, he approached this Court by means of this application under Section 438 Cr.P.C.
Allegations levelled against the applicant are false and based on concocted facts.
Investigating officer has not conducted fair investigation.

Lastly, it is submitted that he has apprehension of imminent arrest and in case, applicant is granted anticipatory bail, he would not misuse the liberty and would cooperate with the trial.
5.
Per contra learned Additional Government Advocate for the state of U.P. opposed the prayer for granting anticipatory bail to the applicant by contending that it is an old matter of the year 2005.
Charge-sheet was submitted in the year 2007 and before submission of charge-sheet, statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. of the applicant was recorded.
Applicant had also preferred writ petition for quashing of the F.I.R. as such applicant was very much aware about the criminal proceeding against him.

He further relying upon the judgements of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of State of Madhya Pradesh Vs. Pradeep Sharma, (2014) 2 SCC 171 and Prem Shankar Prasad Vs. State of Bihar and Another, AIR 2021 SC 5125 submits that since non-bailable warrant has been issued against the applicant since long, therefore, anticipatory bail cannot be granted to the applicant at this stage.

sentences.text: 6. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties, I find substance in the submission of learned A.G.A. for the state that applicant is very much aware about the criminal proceeding against him.

Object of section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, is that a person should not be unnecessarily harassed or humiliated in order to satisfy personal vendetta or grudge of complainant or any other person operating the things directly or from behind the curtains.

It is well settled that discretionary power conferred by the legislature on this court cannot be put in a straitjacket formula, but such discretionary power either grant or refusal of anticipatory bail has to be exercised carefully in appropriate cases with circumspection on the basis of the available material after evaluating the facts of the particular case and considering other relevant factors (nature and gravity Shankarnath Pandey vs State Of U.P. on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187303330/
2 of accusation, role attributed to accused, conduct of accused, criminal antecedents, possibility of the applicant to flee from Justice, apprehension of tampering of the witnesses or threat to the complainant, impact of grant of anticipatory bail in investigation, trial or society, etc.)

entities.text: Shankarnath Pandey vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
with meticulous precision maintaining balance between the conflicting interest, namely, sanctity of individual liberty and interest of society.
7. In the light of above, looking to the facts and circumstances of this case, submissions of learned counsel for the parties, as well as considering the reasons noted above, this court is of the view that no case for exercising its discretionary power under section 438 Code of Criminal Procedure is made out in favour of applicant.
8. Accordingly this application under section 438 Cr.P.C. is rejected.

9. It is clarified that observations made in this order at this stage is limited for the purpose of determination of this anticipatory bail application and will in no way be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
The concerned court below shall be absolutely free to arrive at its independent conclusions according to law on the basis of materials / evidences on record.
